hook.line: Don Hernando is telling you where he drove in his taxi days and where the café sits on the street. Spanish has small frames for along, across and above.
hook.es: Caminamos a lo largo de la playa.

examples.es: Caminamos a lo largo de la playa.
El café está al otro lado de la calle.
examples.en: The café is on the other side of the street.

examples.es: Llovió mucho a lo largo del año.
examples.en: It rained a lot throughout the year.

examples.es: Hay árboles a lo largo de la calle.
examples.en: There are trees along the street.

examples.es: El cartel está en lo alto del edificio.
examples.en: The sign is at the top of the building.

examples.es: ¿Qué hay al otro lado de la calle?
examples.en: What is on the other side of the street?

rule:
Four small frames, each followed by a place.

*A lo largo de* follows something from end to end, in space or in time: *a lo largo de la playa*, *a lo largo del año*.

*Al otro lado de* means on the other side of.

*En lo alto de* means at the top of.

Watch *de* plus *el*: it becomes *del*, as in *a lo largo del año*.

English uses "along", "across" and "throughout" for this. Spanish keeps the same frame each time.
smallPrint: Teachers call these prepositional phrases: several words that work together as one preposition.

readAndPick.es: Caminamos a lo largo de la playa.
options: We walked along the beach.
We walked to the beach.
We walked across the beach.

readAndPick.es: El café está al otro lado de la calle.
options: The café is on this side of the street.
The café is on the other side of the street.
The café is on the street.

readAndPick.es: Llovió mucho a lo largo del año.
options: It rained a lot at the end of the year.
It rained a lot yesterday.
It rained a lot throughout the year.

readAndPick.es: El cartel está en lo alto del edificio.
options: The sign is at the top of the building.
The sign is inside the building.
The sign is next to the building.

readAndPick.es: Hay árboles a lo largo de la calle.
options: There are trees on the other side of the street.
There are trees along the street.
There are trees at the top of the street.

readAndPick.es: ¿Qué hay al otro lado de la calle?
options: What is on the other side of the street?
What is at the top of the street?
What is along the street?

readAndPick.es: Vale vive al otro lado de la plaza.
options: Vale lives in the square.
Vale lives near the square.
Vale lives on the other side of the square.

readAndPick.es: Don Hernando manejó a lo largo de la avenida.
options: Don Hernando drove along the avenue.
Don Hernando drove to the avenue.
Don Hernando drove across the avenue.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Hay árboles ___ la calle.* (*a lo largo de* or *al otro lado de*) There are trees along the street.
yourTurn.answer: Hay árboles a lo largo de la calle.
yourTurn.why: Trees all the way down the street: *a lo largo de*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *El café está ___ la calle.* (*al otro lado de* or *en lo alto de*) The café is on the other side of the street.
yourTurn.answer: El café está al otro lado de la calle.
yourTurn.why: The far side of the street is *al otro lado de*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: We walked along the beach.
yourTurn.answer: Caminamos a lo largo de la playa.
yourTurn.why: *A lo largo de* follows the beach from end to end.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: It rained a lot throughout the year.
yourTurn.answer: Llovió mucho a lo largo del año.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: The sign is at the top of the building.
yourTurn.answer: El cartel está en lo alto del edificio.
yourTurn.why: *En lo alto de* means at the top of, and *de el* becomes *del*.

yourTurn.prompt: Ask: What is on the other side of the street?
yourTurn.answer: ¿Qué hay al otro lado de la calle?

yourTurn.prompt: Say: Vale lives on the other side of the square.
yourTurn.answer: Vale vive al otro lado de la plaza.
yourTurn.why: The same *al otro lado de* frame, with a new place.

pitfalls.wrong: Caminamos a lo largo la playa.
pitfalls.right: Caminamos a lo largo de la playa.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The frame always ends in *de* before the place.

pitfalls.wrong: El café está a otro lado de la calle.
pitfalls.right: El café está al otro lado de la calle.
pitfalls.why: It is *al otro lado*: *a* plus *el* joined, and the article stays.

pitfalls.wrong: Llovió mucho a lo largo de el año.
pitfalls.right: Llovió mucho a lo largo del año.

personal: Think of a street or a trip you know. Say something true about it with *a lo largo de…* or *al otro lado de…*
